glosses: to sing (of), to glorify, to celebrate
прославить, изобразить — обычно в торжественных стихах, песнях и т. п. — героев, события, чувства

examples.text: Воспой нам песнь любви и брани, // О скальд, свидетель древних лет, // Твой меч тяжёл для слабой длани, // Но глас века переживет!

glosses: To exalt, or give glory or praise to (something or someone).
To make (something) appear to be more glorious than it is; regard something or someone as excellent baselessly.

examples.text: Some movies glorify mobsters by making them seem like the cool kids around the block.
Historical dictators are glorified in some countries that are dictatorships and by some political radicals.
Thursday's long-awaited relocation fulfils a key pledge of the socialist government, which said Spain should not continue to glorify a fascist who ruled the country for nearly four decades.

glosses: To worship or extol.
Antiphon.
A choral or vocal composition, often with a religious or political lyric.

examples.text: The school's anthem sang of its many outstanding qualities, and it was hard to keep a straight face while singing.

glosses: A hymn of praise or loyalty.

examples.text: The choir sang a selection of Christmas anthems at the service just before the big day.

glosses: A very popular song or track.

examples.text: In May 2000, they even finally cracked the UK top ten when they teamed up with Paul Van Dyk on the trance anthem "The Riddle"...

glosses: To celebrate with anthems.

examples.text: [T]hou shalt hear / Distant harvest-carols clear; / Rustle of the reaped corn; / Sweet birds antheming the morn: [...]

glosses: To produce musical or harmonious sounds with one’s voice.

examples.text: "I really want to sing in the school choir," said Vera.

glosses: To perform a vocal part in a musical composition, regardless of technique.
To express audibly by means of a harmonious vocalization.

examples.text: sing a lullaby
In the lightness of my heart I sang catches of songs as my horse gayly bore me along the well-remembered road.

glosses: To soothe with singing.

examples.text: to sing somebody to sleep

glosses: Of birds, to vocalise:
To produce a 'song', for the purposes of defending a breeding territory or to attract a mate.
Of birds, to vocalise:
To produce any type of melodious vocalisation.

examples.text:
⁠I do but sing because I must,
And pipe but as the linnets sing:
And unto one her note is gay,
⁠For now her little ones have ranged;
⁠And unto one her note is changed,
Because her brood is stol’n away.
The evening was still very warm, and the birds in the woods were singing in praise of spring.

glosses: To confess under interrogation.
To make a small, shrill sound.

examples.text: The air sings in passing through a crevice.
a singing kettle
O'er his head the flying spear / Sang innocent, and spent its force in air.

glosses: To relate in verse; to celebrate in poetry.

examples.text: Again I bid the mournful Goddeſs write / The fond Purſuit of fugitive Delight: / Bid her exalt her melancholy Wing, / And rais'd from Earth, and ſav'd from Paſſion, ſing / Of human Hope by croſs Event deſtroyed, / Of uſeleſs Wealth, and Greatneſs unenjoy'd, […]
Who would not sing for Lycidas? he knew Himself to sing, and build the lofty rhyme.

glosses: To display fine qualities; to stand out as excellent.

examples.text: The sauce really makes this lamb sing.
[Alissa Monte said] “This result was all about demonstrating that LZ [the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment] works, and it does! As we take more data and mature our analyses, we get to make LZ sing. […]”

glosses: To be capable of being sung; to produce a certain effect by being sung.

examples.text: No song sings well unless it is open-vowelled, and has the rhythmic stress on the vowels. Tennyson's songs, for instance, are not generally adapted to music.

glosses: In traditional Aboriginal culture, to direct a supernatural influence on (a person or thing), usually malign; to curse.

examples.text: ‘We sung them two real good. We never give Louis Beck no place to find rest from his torment.’

glosses: To yell or shout.

examples.text: I took my flogging like a stone. If I had sung, some of the convicts would have given me some lush with a locust in it (laudanum hocussing), and when I was asleep would have given me a crack on the head that would have laid me straight.

glosses: The act, or event, of singing songs.

examples.text: I sometimes have a quick sing in the shower.
Then all three would go off in search of the first, give it a good talking to and maybe a bit of a sing as well.
Some of the young folks asked Mrs. Long could they have a sing at her home that Sunday afternoon; she readily agreed, telling them to come early, bring their songbooks, and have a good sing.
'Ah, yes, Miss Fisher, have you had a nice sing?'
